text:
kea: quick follow-up from the dev-front on handoff-proxy: we need to nail teardown semantics for tunnel vs proxy. observed corner where runtime evicts mid-stream and tunnel left client hanging. want ideas for graceful handoff patterns.

marta: ouch. is the eviction from affinity or quota reclaim?

kea: quota reclaim on dedicated pool (preemption). runtime sends eviction signal but TCP tunnel stays open for a bit and requests error out with partial responses.

colin: two immediate options: 1) runtime sends a FIN-with-cause that the client SDK understands and retries on a new runtime; 2) broker/proxy can preemptively mirror stream data to a standby runtime during handoff (heavy).

ryan: option 1 seems simplest. make eviction part of protocol: runtime emits structured frame before termination: {evict:true, reason:"quota", resume_token: "base64"}. SDK can re-establish and resume using token.

kea: agree but must be backward-compatible. older runtimes won't send resume_token. we should define graceful fallback: if no token, SDK retries from start and control-plane may route to cheaper model variant.

marta: nit: avoid exposing model internals in frame. resume_token should be opaque PoP signed by runtime and verifiable by control-plane.

colin: also consider short-lived buffer handoff: proxy can buffer last N tokens for X seconds and attempt to replay to new runtime during switchover. avoids losing small tail. downside: proxy needs to store transient data (sensitive!).

kea: sensitive is a key concern. we prefer not to persist payloads in proxy. could encrypt in-memory and zero after use, but compliance folks will balk.

ryan: what about client-driven reconnect pattern: on any stream error with code STREAM_EVICT, SDK backoff immediate, fetch new route from control-plane, reconnect with resume_token if present. Keep proxy stateless.

marta: adds requirement that control-plane generate route hints fast. control-plane should maintain warm-standby mappings for pinned tenants to reduce reconnection latency.

colin: latency budget: reconnection+resume must be < 250ms for interactive UX. otherwise we need proxy buffering or keep-alive hedging to standby runtime.

kea: hedging idea: for particularly high-SLA tenants we could enable "dual-write" mode at handshake: stream goes to primary runtime, and a thin ack-only connection is kept with a standby for rapid takeover. heavier cost but opt-in and billed.

ryan: agree opt-in billing tag in manifest. sample optional snippet: 

```json
{"runtime":{"handoff":{"mode":"auto","support_resume":true,"cost_profile":"hsa:dual-write"}}}
```

ryan: default remains single-writer to keep costs down.

marta: operationally we need a clear circuit-breaker: if reconnection fails N times, degrade to a fallback model (smaller) rather than block the user. add telemetry for user-visible degradation rate.

colin: security: resume_token must be PoP and short-lived (<=60s). Broker should validate token at handshake, not persist it. Also forbid resume across tenant boundaries obviously.

kea: infra-bot: created task https://infra/issues/hand-off-teardown-432 for canary tests & resume token spec.

infra-bot: checklist: mTLS end-to-end, resume token spec, SDK error codes, perf target for reconnect <250ms, canary plan.

ryan: tests: 1) eviction with resume token (happy path), 2) eviction without token (fallback path), 3) dual-write takeover latency, 4) token replay attempt blocked. I'll own SDK changes.

marta: also add privacy test proving proxy never writes stream payload to disk and that in-memory buffers are zeroed on teardown. Compliance will want an audit.

kea: thanks everyone. i'll draft a compact RFC listing: eviction frames, resume_token format (PoP JWT), opt-in dual-write, billing tag, SDK error codes, and canary plan. will loop back for 72h review.
